title: Durable Objects, Unbound
subtitle: One promised message, a well that learned to say no, and the road to running it yourself
logline: A chat message gets its tick. The machine that gave the tick goes dark. The tick is still true. In a paper-cut harbour town where every machine is a lamp-lit house, a chat room is a lantern and the storage bucket is the town well, the film follows one promised message through every failure that could break it: two houses claiming the room at once, an owner that sleeps and wakes, a crash mid-upload, a successor that dies mid-recovery, a tail that lives only on the neighbours. From Durable Objects in 2020 to the October 2026 commit that began merging celld into workerd, it shows why a bucket that cannot run a line of code can make a room portable, and why it cannot do it alone.

staging.note: Staging appendix (head writer, story stage, 2026-10-31). Fixed geography, hands, text rules, transitions and the shared build list every shot obeys. Spread into script.json by the assembler; film-shots builds the modules in buildList before any shot. Full visual grammar: story/treatment.md.

geography.canonical: HARBOUR TOWN (canonical, night, winterBlue): L0 sky ramp peaking at 58% height; L1 the sea and a low far shore with sparse lamps, moon low-left; L2 the hill ridge with dim terraced roofs; L3 three narrow houses on the terrace, always left to right House A (tall, steep gable, round attic window), House B (wider, one chimney), House C (upper terrace, a dormer); each window lamp is that machine's process (lit = running, guttered = gone); each house has a pulley line sloping down to the wellhead; L4 the square with the Well at the left third and, above the wellhead on an iron frame readable from every window like a town clock, the Plate; L5 cobbles and a stone railing; L6 an iron lamp-post crossing frame right (the occluder for in-chapter wipes). A is always screen-left of the Well, B and C screen-right.

staging.badges: IMPLEMENTATION BADGES (canonical): a small brass tag hangs on every machine that shows a real mechanism, naming whose mechanism it is: 'workerd · 28 Oct' (the supplied commit aa494794), 'workerd · 31 Oct' (snapshot ad78a8fe, alarms and facets), 'celld 0.6.3' (8702f6d), 'Cloudflare, hosted' (the 2024 Storage Relay Service), 'Amazon S3' (the store's own behaviour). A mechanism never carries two badges; workerd's 20 s / 16 s / 12 s lease numbers never appear beside a celld badge; LTX never appears beside a workerd badge. Badges are art, drawn by the sets at ≥ 26 px, and count as one text item only when the narration names them.
staging.pins: THE PIN (canonical): a red-tagged brass pin seated in the machine whose assumption is under test (the Tooth ch03-s02; A's candle-band latch ch05-s04; the keeper's lamp-to-Plate arm ch06-s05; the neighbours' wax-seal stamp ch07-s04). The demonstrator's hand pulls it on the narration's 'pull', the scene replays without it in emberRed, the hand reseats it and the correct run plays in the chapter's mood. Pins hang on a board for the ch08-s01 montage, each in the order it was pulled.

hands.canonical: HANDS (canonical): only the demonstrator's hand (cast narrator-hands) reaches into the town from outside, always from the lower RIGHT, and only to pull or reseat a pin, to turn a Plate tile in a parchment insert, or to hold up a slip. Keepers' hands act inside the town (claims, scissors, scrolls, bells). Real people's hands stay at their desks and never touch the town.
hands.module: sets/demonstratorHand.ts: a rolled-sleeve forearm sprite with pinch / grip / point variants, sliding in on twos along a shallow arc

staging.textRule: TEXT RULE (canonical): besides the date stamp and name cards, at most two text items per shot, one per beat; labels ≤ 42 characters; quotes verbatim from research/quotes.json, short, attributed, never set in full while also spoken in full; trade terms named once with a 'term' tag; no code identifiers in speech (on a parchment plate an exact identifier may appear once, expanded aloud); the BOTTOM 12% OF THE FRAME (y > 634 of 720) carries no text and no key action (captions live there).
staging.transitions: TRANSITIONS (canonical): chapter starts iris open on the Room Lantern or a desk lamp; era moves ink-bleed; every parchment insert paper-folds in and out; failures enter and leave by lampChange (emberRed), never crossfade; in-chapter wipes use the L6 lamp-post occluder; otherwise cut on the idea (the Tooth's click or thunk, the bell).
staging.accentBudget: ACCENTS: one warm practical per shot (the Room Lantern or a desk lamp) plus the brass of the Plate and Tooth; serverCyan only inside the Well cutaway, the hosted-relay diagram and the commit strip; red only for pins, wax seals and emberRed failure grades.

creditsSources.text: That object exists in only one location in the whole world at a time. — Kenton Varda, 2020
Once at least three of these followers respond that they have received the change, SRS informs the application that the write is confirmed. — Kenton Varda, 2024
This component acts as a witness to writes, notified every time an object changes. — Werner Vogels, 2021
With celld, I wanted the opposite: one binary, written in Rust, with object storage as its only external service dependency. — Ryan Dahl, 2026
This is the beginning of merging celld's functionality into workerd. — Ryan Dahl, commit aa494794, 2026

staging.sourcesCard: SOURCES CARD (end): Cloudflare blog posts by Kenton Varda (2020, 2021, 2022, 2024) and by Ryan Dahl and Kenton Varda (2026); Deno blog (Ryan Dahl, 2026); AWS announcements (Dec 2020, Aug 2024, Nov 2024) and S3 User Guide; Werner Vogels, 'Diving Deep on S3 Consistency' (2021); SQLite file format; workerd at aa494794 and ad78a8fe; celld 0.6.3 at 8702f6d. celld's replicator descends from rustyriver (Mike Nomitch), Litestream (Ben Johnson) and the LTX format. Harbour, room, message, houses and epoch numbers are illustrative. Upstream tests were read, not run.

buildList.note: Shared, data-driven set and machine modules for apps/bookshelf/src/viz/films/durable-objects-unbound/sets/, built and contact-sheeted before any shot so scale, colour code and placement cannot drift. Each takes explicit state, and draws nothing not bound to a real quantity (style bible §6).

staging.runtime: Story stage estimate at the house 140 wpm; the narrator's measured wpm replaces it after voice casting (voice/voice.json).
staging.fixtures: FIXTURE CONTINUITY (canonical, illustrative): message #42 'the ferry is late' sent from the sender's harbour-side window on L4 right of the Well; House A owns the room at epoch 7 (A·7·from 7); on the night A goes dark House B claims epoch 8 and dies before opening (its window flickers once in ch01-s02, paid off aloud in ch05-s06); House C claims epoch 9 from 7 and recovers epoch 7 (ch07-s01 Plate C·9·from 7, from tile turns to 9 on opening). Pin-out counterfactuals (ch05-s04, ch06-s05) replay with B at epoch 8 and are labelled by the emberRed grade. In celld's town (ch07-s02..s07) the successor is House C's node; its own notebook is one of the two recovery reads.

runtimeCeilingNote: 2026-10-31: the brief allows 20–28 minutes; the authorized hard ceiling is 28 minutes (1680 s), with a 24-minute target. Story estimate at 140 wpm; the locked voice wpm replaces it.
